Topics · Who was Muhammad?

Did someone secretly teach Muhammad the Quran?

The Quran keeps the charge, names no one, and answers. The full objection, the answer, and the limits of each.

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ إِنْ هَـٰذَآ إِلَّآ إِفْكٌ ٱفْتَرَىٰهُ وَأَعَانَهُۥ عَلَيْهِ قَوْمٌ ءَاخَرُونَ ۖ فَقَدْ جَآءُو ظُلْمًا وَزُورًا٤ وَقَالُوٓا۟ أَسَـٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ ٱكْتَتَبَهَا فَهِىَ تُمْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا٥﴾

Translation of the meaning

And those who disbelieve say, "This [Qur’ān] is not except a falsehood he invented, and another people assisted him in it." But they have committed an injustice and a lie. And they say, "Legends of the former peoples which he has written down, and they are dictated to him morning and afternoon."

Quran · Al-Furqan 25:4-5

The two verses do not soften the charge: a fabrication, and others helped him. Old tales written down for him, dictated morning and evening. Look at what the objection holds. First, as quoted, it gives no name. Second, it describes daily work: morning and evening, for years, in a small town that was watching. Third, it looks for a source outside him, so they did not see this as what they knew of him. Three observations, and none of them an answer yet.

A question for you

What would you expect of a charge like this if it were strong?

If you sayThat it name the teacher.
ThenA reasonable measure, and the Quran keeps the charge with no name. The Quran may simply not repeat one, so do not rest everything on this alone.
If you sayThat it show how the knowledge passed.
ThenThe third part asks that, of time and place.
If you sayThe name does not matter. The likelihood is enough.
ThenThat is the position of some historians today, and it deserves weighing. The third part takes it seriously.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَلَقَدْ نَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّمَا يُعَلِّمُهُۥ بَشَرٌ ۗ لِّسَانُ ٱلَّذِى يُلْحِدُونَ إِلَيْهِ أَعْجَمِىٌّ وَهَـٰذَا لِسَانٌ عَرَبِىٌّ مُّبِينٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We certainly know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches him [i.e., the Prophet (ﷺ)]." The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign,[715] and this [recitation, i.e., Qur’ān] is [in] a clear Arabic language.

Translator's notes

[715] Having seen the Prophet (ﷺ) speaking with a foreign man on occasion, the Quraysh accused him of repeating the man's words.

Quran · An-Nahl 16:103

The answer comes in one verse. We know what they say: only a human teaches him. Then: the speech of the one they point to is foreign, and this is clear Arabic. The answer is about language: the one you accuse does not speak this Arabic. It is a sharp reply, with a limit: a teacher can pass on meaning while a student shapes the words. So the verse answers the part about the tongue. The question left is who shaped this Arabic.

A question for you

How much does this answer weigh with you?

If you sayIt settles the question of the wording.
ThenThen the content remains, and the next part reaches it.
If you sayNot enough: meaning can be passed on.
ThenThat is the strongest objection to the verse, and it stands. The next part stays with it.
If you sayI cannot judge the Arabic.
ThenAn honest reply, and the point does weigh more for those who know the Arabic. A Step takes that up.

Part 3 of 3

﴿قُلْ أَنزَلَهُ ٱلَّذِى يَعْلَمُ ٱلسِّرَّ فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ غَفُورًا رَّحِيمًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, [O Muḥammad], "It has been revealed by He who knows [every] secret within the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful."

Quran · Al-Furqan 25:6

﴿وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ رُوحًا مِّنْ أَمْرِنَا ۚ مَا كُنتَ تَدْرِى مَا ٱلْكِتَـٰبُ وَلَا ٱلْإِيمَـٰنُ وَلَـٰكِن جَعَلْنَـٰهُ نُورًا نَّهْدِى بِهِۦ مَن نَّشَآءُ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ۚ وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِىٓ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And thus We have revealed to you an inspiration of Our command [i.e., the Qur’ān]. You did not know what is the Book or [what is] faith, but We have made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. And indeed, [O Muḥammad], you guide to a straight path -

Quran · Ash-Shura 42:52

Translation

He led them also by a straight way, that they might go to a city to live in.

Original · Hebrew

וַ֭יַּֽדְרִיכֵם בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ יְשָׁרָ֑ה לָ֝לֶ֗כֶת אֶל־עִ֥יר מוֹשָֽׁב׃

the Psalms · 107:7

World English Bible

Take the objection at its strongest. Few today picture secret lessons. They picture a lifetime of hearing, in a land with Jews, Christians and travellers. That is possible, and the record cannot rule it out. The Quran answers in one line: it was sent down by the One who knows the secret. What remains to weigh: no book recited, no teacher the book names, a life they knew, the breadth of what came, one message with all the prophets. Hearing may explain a line. Would it explain all this?

A question for you

Which explains what you see better?

If you sayHearing from those around him.
ThenThen weigh what that explanation needs: a source, depth, Arabic, breadth. A Step on copying takes it further.
If you sayWhat the Quran says of itself.
ThenThen the next question is whether you can see it agreeing with the books before it.
If you sayI am still weighing.
ThenA good place to stay. His life among them is another strand to weigh.

The same in the other books

Translation

Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.

Original · Hebrew

נֵר־לְרַגְלִ֥י דְבָרֶ֑ךָ וְ֝א֗וֹר לִנְתִיבָתִֽי׃

the Psalms · 119:105

World English Bible

Your reflection

What is the harshest thing said of something you hold dear, and how would you wish to answer it?
